title: MicroDash - latency attribution & trace matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact operator dashboard concept (MicroDash) focused on fast latency attribution and trace anchoring for tokenized inference flows. The goal is a lightweight, low-query, high-signal panel set that on-call and SREs can load on mobile or low-bandwidth terminals during incidents and run routine triage without expensive analytic queries.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: tokenized LLM inference pipelines (request parsing -> routing -> model exec -> kv-cache -> response postprocessing).
- Not covered: long-term historical trend platform (that remains in full dashboards). MicroDash is for immediate investigation and narrow-scope rollouts.
- Performance constraint: the dashboard must render with <=1s median render time in our staging telemetry tier and use <=250 interactive queries per 5-minute refresh for the default panel set.
- Cost constraint: per-incident query budget of 30 credits (query-cost accounting) for mobile use.

High-level goals:
1) Surface the dominant latency contributor quickly (within top 3 suspects)
2) Provide pinned trace links with appropriate context (session id, model version, route policy)
3) Keep metric cardinality low and rely on sampled traces + precomputed aggregates for hot paths
4) Offer a compact drill path: aggregated panel -> 1-click trace -> sample replay snippet

Key metrics (definitions and recommended aggregation):
- user_request_p50_ms / user_request_p95_ms / user_request_p99_ms: end-to-end request duration from API ingress to final byte streamed. Aggregation: percentile over 5m by tenant-weighted sampling. Tagging: tenant_id (hashed), route, model_name, model_variant.
- model_exec_ms: time spent in GPU/CPU model execution excluding queue. Derived by trace span named model.exec.duration. Aggregation: p50/p95 over 5m, rollup by model_variant.
- queue_wait_ms: time spent waiting for execution capacity. Span: scheduler.queue_wait. Use avg and p95.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: (kv_cache_hits / (kv_cache_hits + kv_cache_misses)) as a percentage. Window: 5m. Low cardinality: only by model_variant.
- token_stream_first_byte_ms: time from model output start to first byte delivered to client. Useful to separate model startup vs streaming. Aggregation: p50/p95.
- retry_rate_pct: percent of requests that triggered a fallback/retry path in the last 5m. Tagging: route, fallback_reason.

Tracing anchors and span contract notes:
- Required top-level trace tags for all spans: trace_id, session_id, request_id, tenant_hash, route, model_name, model_version, node_id. These enable consistent stitching in MicroDash.
- Span naming conventions for MicroDash:
  - api.ingest (ingress parsing + auth)
  - router.resolve (routing decision, policy evaluation)
  - scheduler.queue_wait (time before scheduling)
  - model.exec (actual model time)
  - kvcache.lookup (kv cache op, include hit/miss flag)
  - stream.write (stream chunk writes to client)
  - postproc.normalize (any output normalization/hallucination checks)
- Span attributes: model.exec must include seq_len, num_tokens_generated, compute_kind (fp16/fp32/int8), and quant_profile. kvcache.lookup should include key_size and hit boolean.
- Sampling guidance: Keep trace sampling for MicroDash at 1% system-wide, but apply deterministic higher sampling (10–20%) for traces that exceed any of these thresholds: model_exec_ms > model.exec_p95, queue_wait_ms > 2x baseline, or retry_rate triggered. This preserves low cost while ensuring noisy traces surface quickly.

MicroDash panels (compact set, ordered for fastest triage):
1) Topline latency slice row (single horizontal compact panel): p50/p95/p99 of user_request in a single line with colored change indicators vs baseline.
2) Attribution waterfall (small sparklines + percent contribution): split request duration into api.ingest, router.resolve, scheduler.queue_wait, model.exec, postproc.normalize. Shows percentage and delta vs baseline.
3) Model hotspot map (heat cell): model_variant x route showing median model_exec_ms; colored by p95. Click cell -> prefiltered traces.
4) KV cache overview (single small gauge + time series): global kv_cache_hit_ratio and a small 1-line sparkline for last 15m.
5) Fast traces table (sampled, 10 rows): columns {timestamp, tenant_hash, request_id, route, model_variant, dominant_span, duration_ms, trace_link}. 1-click copy request_id, open trace.
6) Recent fallback/retry table: top 5 reasons and counts.
7) Query cost meter: shows remaining incident query budget and approximate credits used in last 5m.

Low-cardinality design rules:
- Only allow tenant_hash, route, model_variant as interactive dimensions on MicroDash. Other dimensions should be hidden in full dashboards.
- Precompute small aggregates in a dedicated MicroDash materialized view (5m rollup) to avoid high-cardinality live queries. Materialized view keys: {minute_bucket, route, model_variant}.
- Avoid free-text filters and heavy joins in panel queries. Use short-lived key-value lookup service for tenant metadata instead.

Investigation flow (operator recipe):
1) Open MicroDash for the affected region/cluster. Check Topline latency slice.
2) If a spike, open Attribution waterfall. If model.exec dominates, click Model hotspot map and open traces for the worst cell. If scheduler.queue_wait dominates, escalate to infra with the queue profile.
3) Use the Fast traces table to copy request_id and paste into prompt-replay tool (if available).
4) If kv_cache_hit_ratio fell, check fallback/retry table and correlate with recent deploys (model_version).

Acceptance criteria for rollout to prod:
- MicroDash renders fully (all 7 panels) within 1.2s median under staging load test (10 concurrent mobile clients).
- Average query cost per full-panel refresh <= 20 credits.
- 95% of produced traces from MicroDash sampling include the required span tags for correct stitching.
- Operators can execute the Investigation flow end-to-end in <3 minutes on first try (observed in usability session).

Migration plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (dev sandbox): implement materialized view and backend endpoints; smoke test queries.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable MicroDash for internal SRE team with synthetic traffic and monitor cost/latency.
- Phase 2 (region rollout): enable for one prod region; add query-cost meter and incident budgeting.
- Phase 3 (org rollout): enable for all regions and include on-call rotation runbook.

Open questions / known tradeoffs:
- Precompute cadence vs freshness: 1m rollups reduce query cost but miss short spikes. We recommend 30s rollup if storage/compute allows.
- Sampling config complexity: deterministic higher sampling for anomalies requires extra control plane hooks. We need a small feature flag to tune sampling windows per region.
- Tenant privacy: tenant_hash must be non-reversible. Confirm hashing scheme with security team before rollout.

Next steps and owners:
- Build materialized view prototype: Arjun (ENGOBS-3472)
- Implement span attribute enforcement in model-serving SDK: Maya (PR: github.com/redwood/serving-sdk/pull/215)
- Small UX wireframe and mobile render test: Tomás
- Security review for tenant hashing: Lena

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on cardinality to keep MicroDash reliable and cheap for incidents. Feedback welcome on which panels are must-have vs nice-to-have for first-pass rollout.
summary: A compact operator dashboard spec that prioritizes quick latency attribution and low query cost for LLM inference. Defines metric contracts, trace anchors, panels, sampling rules, and a phased rollout plan.
